Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cdzoo (development version)

  • The package has a logo.
  • README carries status badges and lists related packages.
  • CI runs lintr (report-only) and test coverage.

cdzoo 0.2.0

New features

  • A sufficient statistic is now a first-class discovery input. cd_method gains an accepts field ("data" or "suffstat"), and the constraint methods pc_suffstat, fci_suffstat, and ggm_suffstat are registered so they appear in list_methods() (which gains an accepts column) and are routable by cd_auto(). A "suffstat" method can also be run on a data matrix through cd_discover(), which reduces the data to its sufficient statistic first.
  • cd_auto() accepts a sufficient statistic, cd_suffstat(C, n), and routes it among the sufficient-statistic methods. A correlation matrix carries only the latent-structure hint, so the recommendation states plainly that the non-Gaussianity, nonlinearity, and equal-variance tests could not be run – which is what an aggregated input does and does not support. report, mode = "consensus", and manifest emission all work on this input.
  • cd_explain() prints a readable account of a recommendation – the method and status, the routing rationale and confidence, the alternatives considered, the thresholds that decided the route, and (for a consensus) the per-edge agreement – the auditable companion to the compact print().
  • cd_auto(mode = "consensus") now draws a family-diverse panel of methods rather than several near-identical members of one family, for a better-grounded agreement signal, and cd_edges(res, agreement = TRUE) reports the per-edge agreement of a consensus result.
  • cd_benchmark(mc.cores = ) runs the scenario grid across cores. Each cell is deterministic given its scenario seed and independent of the others, so the result is identical for any core count.
  • A plot() method for cd_result draws the recovered graph (variables on a circle, arrows for directed edges) using base graphics only – no plotting back-end required.
  • A second vignette, Discovery from sufficient statistics, works an example from co-occurrence counts through a correlation matrix, discovery, a routed recommendation, and a verifiable manifest.

Bug fixes

  • cd_auto()‘s two decline outcomes ("no back-end installed" and "recommendation only (report = FALSE)", including the sufficient- statistic route) now stamp the returned cd_result with classed decline markers ("orchestra_refusal" and "cdzoo_abstention", prepended to the class vector) instead of reporting the decline only as a plain status string. What is declined is unchanged; a caller can now also recognise the decline by class, matching the orchestra packages’ is_orchestra_decline() gate convention.
  • The confidence label a route reports is now revised when the route’s preferred method is not installed and a substitute runs instead: one step down the high/moderate/low ladder for a plain substitution, a second step when the substitute’s declared assumptions contradict the data signature that fired the route (for example a route that fired on non-Gaussian data, substituted with a method that assumes Gaussian margins). The downgrade and its reason are stated in the recommendation’s rationale (CD-03).
  • cd_auto(mode = "route", report = TRUE) no longer errors when the only available method accepts a sufficient statistic rather than raw data (the base installation, where ggm_suffstat is always available): the final route call now reduces the input through .method_input() like every other call site (CD-02).

Documentation

  • Both vignettes (A benchmark harness and recommender for causal discovery and Discovery from sufficient statistics) are rewritten to the orchestra vignette quality bar: each opens with the adjustment-set question an analyst who does not trust a single algorithm would ask, follows the fixed Why/What/Do/Read/Limits/What to read next/Reproduce shape, reads the recommender’s rationale, confidence and alternatives from a live cd_auto() call rather than describing them, and adds a ggplot2 figure each table cannot replace (a consensus edge-agreement heat map; a recovered-graph-versus-known-truth comparison drawn from the adjacency matrix).
  • The vignette’s benchmark figures (fig-accuracy, fig-speed) now carry fig.cap captions and each is followed by a sentence interpreting what it shows, including a grounded comparison of the kernel conditional- independence method’s runtime against the LiNGAM family (CD-07).
  • A comma splice in the vignette’s benchmark-summary paragraph is now two independent clauses joined correctly (CD-20).
  • The registry count is corrected from “sixteen” (the method count before 0.2.0’s sufficient-statistic methods) to “nineteen registered methods, sixteen of them benchmarked” in README.md and CONSTELLATION_MEMBER.md (CD-10); the README’s purpose paragraph now precedes the badges block (CD-19).
  • plot.cd_result is now indexed in _pkgdown.yml’s reference section (CD-15).
  • orchestra_manifest, the one exported S7 class with no worked example, now has one showing construction via as_orchestra_manifest() and inspection of the resulting object.

cdzoo 0.1.1

Breaking changes

  • The federation manifest’s integrity hash is now computed over version-stable bytes (serialisation pinned to format 2, its version-carrying header dropped before hashing), matching the updated reference contract (MANIFEST_VERSION 2.0.0-draft). A manifest emitted under one R version now verifies under any other. Manifests emitted before this change no longer verify and must be re-emitted:

    # before: verify_manifest(old_manifest)$ok could be FALSE on another R version
# after:  re-emit from the original result
m <- as_orchestra_manifest(result)
verify_manifest(m)$ok

  • cd_result@alternatives now always holds method labels, in both "route" and "consensus" modes; the consensus member results moved to provenance$runs:

    # before: con@alternatives held cd_result objects in consensus mode
# after:
con <- cd_auto(x, mode = "consensus")
con@alternatives       # method labels
con@provenance$runs    # the member cd_result objects

Minor improvements and fixes

  • cd_auto() records the four data-characteristic thresholds that decided the route in the result’s provenance$thresholds, and documents them, so every recommendation carries the rule it was made under.

  • cd_discover_suffstat() runs an order-independent ("stable") skeleton search on the Fisher-Z branch too, so the recovered graph no longer depends on the variable ordering; it rejects a covariance with a non-positive diagonal, and the Gaussian-graphical-model skeleton refuses a matrix too ill-conditioned to invert rather than returning noise.

  • cd_correlation_from_counts() rejects negative, missing, or duplicated pairwise counts instead of silently mishandling them.

  • The Python back-end availability check is passive and memoised: cdzoo never initialises Python (which can trigger interpreter provisioning) just to report availability. Back-ends show as installed once reticulate’s interpreter is initialised or configured; options(cdzoo.python_init = TRUE) opts into eager initialisation, and list_methods(refresh = TRUE) re-probes after a mid-session install.

  • The scenario simulators now draw their noise under the documented scenario seed (previously a lazy-evaluation quirk drew it under the graph-derived stream, coupling the noise to the graph settings). Scenario realisations at a fixed seed change accordingly; the scenario truths are unaffected.

  • cd_score() normalises its inputs so any non-zero entry counts as an edge mark – a weighted adjacency matrix now scores its orientations too – and skeleton_f1 is NA (previously 0) when the truth has no edges, where recall is undefined.

  • cd_diagnose() – and therefore cd_auto()’s routing – is now deterministic and leaves the caller’s random-number state untouched: on large data sets the normality and regression heuristics read an evenly spaced, deterministic subsample instead of a random one. Repeated calls on the same data return the same characteristics and the same recommendation.

  • cd_scenario() accepts any finite seed; seeds above about 271,000 previously failed with an integer-overflow error. Realisations at all previously-valid seeds are unchanged.

  • cd_auto(report = FALSE) now labels its result "recommendation only (report = FALSE)" instead of "ok", so a recommendation-only result – and the manifest it emits – states that no graph was recovered.

  • cd_benchmark() now warns about requested methods it drops (an unknown id, an absent back-end, or a cost above cost_limit) instead of dropping them silently.

  • The citation file reads the version from the installed package rather than hard-coding it, and the pkgdown reference index gained the sufficient-statistic and federation-manifest functions added in 0.1.0.

cdzoo 0.1.0

New features

  • cd_discover_suffstat() runs constraint-based discovery directly on a sufficient statistic – a correlation or covariance matrix and its sample size – and returns a cd_result in the same amat.cpdag convention as cd_discover(). This is cdzoo’s front door for data that arrives already aggregated (a published correlation matrix, a privacy-preserving summary, or pairwise co-occurrence counts) with no row-level observation matrix to pass to cd_discover(). method = "ggm" returns the partial-correlation (Gaussian-graphical-model) skeleton and needs no back-end; method = "pc" and method = "fci" add orientation through pcalg, with "fci" allowing latent confounders.
  • A magnitude-based conditional-independence test (test = "magnitude") prunes an edge when the partial-correlation magnitude falls below tau, the correct behaviour at population sample sizes where a significance test (test = "gauss", the default) would call every pair dependent.
  • cd_correlation_from_counts() assembles a positive-definite correlation matrix from pairwise binary two-by-two counts (the phi coefficient, base R, or the latent-Gaussian tetrachoric correlation via the optional psych package), repairing an indefinite matrix to the nearest positive-definite correlation matrix by eigenvalue clipping. Its output feeds straight into cd_discover_suffstat(), so the whole counts -> correlation -> discovery -> as_orchestra_manifest() path composes.

cdzoo 0.0.0.9000

  • Initial development version. cdzoo provides a single typed interface over a portfolio of causal-discovery algorithms drawn from several R and Python back-ends, a structural-causal-model scenario grid with known ground truth, fair graph-recovery metrics, and an evidence-routed recommender.

Features

  • cd_discover() runs one registered method and returns a cd_result carrying the recovered graph in a single amat.cpdag adjacency convention, with timing and status.
  • cd_auto() inspects a data set’s characteristics with cd_diagnose(), routes it to a method suited to that regime, runs the best installed method on the route, and reports its rationale and a confidence label. mode = "consensus" returns a stability-weighted union of several methods with per-edge agreement. Given an evaluable density rather than a sample – a proxymix mixture or target – it reads the conditional-independence structure off the mixture in closed form.
  • list_methods() and register_method() expose and extend the registry of sixteen built-in methods, drawn from pcalg, bnlearn, and Python back-ends reached through reticulate. Each method is gated on its back-end, so the harness, scenarios, metrics, and routing logic run with no suggested package installed.
  • cd_scenario() and cd_scenarios() generate benchmark data from known DAGs, and cd_score() and cd_benchmark() score recovered graphs with skeleton F1, structural Hamming distance, and orientation recall.
  • cd_field_benchmark ships a summary of the sixteen methods across the nine scenarios, the evidence behind the recommender’s routing preferences.
  • as_orchestra_manifest() adapts a cd_result into a versioned, integrity-hashed orchestra_manifest (inferential_target = "structure"): the recovered edges ride in params, and the method, routing rationale, confidence, and single-method-versus-consensus flag ride in the typed summary and metadata, so a recovered graph can be passed downstream with its provenance and verified with verify_manifest().
